transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Well, what brings me in is... I keep hearing these clear voices. Mostly in my apartment, but sometimes when I'm at the museum, too, in the empty rooms. It sounds like women whispering, right from behind the walls, telling me which photographs belong in the archive. I used to go to the museum every Tuesday, actually, because the crowds were thinner. My husband, before he passed, he hated museums. He always said his feet hurt, but I think he just didn't like standing still. He was a salesman, you know, always moving, always talking. He could sell ice to an Eskimo, that man. We had this lovely little car, a Buick, and he'd drive us all over the state on weekends... but yes, the voices. They just keep whispering about the photographs.
Do the voices ever say things that make you feel like people are watching you or trying to harm you?

Well, they don't say that exactly, but... but I know they are. I mean, the museum board and the city arts people, they've been monitoring my phone. I'm absolutely convinced of it. They know my Caribbean archive will completely change how the galleries tell the truth, and they just can't have that. No one has shown me a single shred of proof that they aren't listening in. My husband used to say you can never trust the city council, either. Back in the eighties, they tried to rezone our neighborhood, and he went down to town hall and gave them a piece of his mind. He wore this awful plaid suit that day, the one I tried to throw out twice, but he said it was his lucky suit. He wore it when he closed the biggest deal of his career with that paper company... anyway, yes, the museum people are definitely watching me because of the archive.
Are there times when you believe something strongly that others around you do not seem to understand or agree with, even when there's no evidence to support it?

Well, yes, exactly what I was just saying! I mean, I am absolutely convinced the museum board and the city arts people are monitoring my phone. They know about my Caribbean archive, and they know it's going to completely change how the galleries tell the truth. My sister, she thinks I'm making it up. She told me I was being ridiculous just last week when we were having tea. She always drinks chamomile, says it calms her nerves, but I prefer Earl Grey. A good strong cup of Earl Grey is what you need in the afternoon. We used to have it on the porch when we were girls, back when the old oak tree was still standing in the front yard. Lightning struck it in '98, split it right down the middle. It was a shame, really, it provided such wonderful shade... but yes, nobody agrees with me about the phones. But no one has shown me a single thing that proves they aren't listening. They just say I'm imagining it, but I know they're watching me.
Do you believe that the things you're working on, like your Caribbean archive, are so important that others are trying to stop you because of their significance?

Well, yes, that's exactly what I've been saying! The archive is monumental. It's going to completely change how the galleries tell the truth, and they just cannot have that. That's exactly why the museum board and the city arts people are monitoring my phone, to stop me. And like I said, no one has shown me a single scrap of proof that they aren't listening in. 

I can even hear these little clicks on the line sometimes. We used to have this heavy, mustard-yellow rotary phone in the kitchen, back in our first house, and it would click just like that when the dial got stuck. It had a cord so long you could walk all the way into the dining room while you were talking. My husband used to trip over that cord at least twice a week when he was hunting for a midnight snack. He loved those little powdered donuts, you know, the ones that come in the crinkly cellophane sleeves? He would get powdered sugar all over his chin and down the front of his bathrobe... he had this terrible, heavy maroon bathrobe that he refused to throw away. He just wore it to absolute tatters, even when the pockets started falling off. 

But, um... yes, the significance of it. They know how important the Caribbean archive is, and they are absolutely trying to stop me.
Do you ever hear the voices even when you're not thinking about the museum or your archive project?

Well, the voices... yes, I do hear them. Mostly it's when I'm in my apartment, or sometimes when I'm walking through the empty rooms at the museum. It's these clear voices, like women whispering right from behind the walls. They tell me exactly which photographs belong in the archive, which ones are the truth. 

It reminds me of the whispering gallery at the old science center we used to take the kids to on rainy weekends. You could stand in one corner and whisper, and someone all the way across the room could hear you clear as a bell. The kids thought it was absolute magic. My daughter, Sarah, she used to wear these little red patent leather shoes with a buckle, and they would click-clack on the marble floors of that science center. She refused to wear sneakers, even when we went to the park. She'd be out there on the jungle gym in her Sunday best, getting grass stains all over her ruffled socks. I spent a fortune on stain remover back then. The one in the blue bottle, with the little scrubber brush attached to the top? It never really worked on the grass stains, but it was wonderful for getting tomato sauce out of my husband's ties. He was a terribly messy eater, especially when we had spaghetti... 

But yes, the whispering women behind the walls. They just keep telling me which photographs to pick.
